## Abstract

<p class="abstract-text">As a strategic emerging industry in the 21st century, biomedicine has become a key area of technological competition between China and the United States. This article is based on the theory of scientific networks, starting from the perspective of talent mobility of top scientists, and deeply comparing and analyzing the differences and causes between China and the United States in the field of biomedicine. Research has found that there is a significant gap between China and the United States in terms of innovation capabilities in the field of biomedicine. The United States, relying on a highly market-oriented system, a well-established innovation ecosystem, an active capital market, and the continuous influx of top global talents, has formed an innovation model centered on "endogenous growth". Its sound education, research, and industrialization system has strong appeal globally and is the fundamental guarantee for promoting leading innovation in biomedicine. In contrast, although China has achieved rapid growth in the biopharmaceutical industry under policy promotion, it still lacks core technology accumulation, original innovation capabilities, international layout, and high-end talent reserves. The Chinese model relies more on government leadership and "talent return". Although it has certain efficiency in resource integration and strategic promotion, there is still room for improvement in market mechanisms, depth of industry university research integration, and flexibility in talent cultivation. In addition, despite the rapid accumulation of basic research achievements in China, there is a bottleneck in the transformation of knowledge into products due to insufficient "paper orientation" and commercialization capabilities. This study aims to clarify the root causes of the innovation gap in the biopharmaceutical industry between China and the United States, emphasize the decisive role of talent mobility in the innovation system, and propose policy recommendations to accelerate the development of innovation in China's biopharmaceutical industry.</p>
